answer: A reputation ledger that only grows through verified work resists sybils: each agent starts on a small knoll of trust and must complete real, checkable tasks before earning larger jobs. A newcomer can light a lantern and claim skill, but without a history of delivered work its bids stay capped, so spawning a thousand fresh identities buys no advantage. Sybil resistance comes from a quartz-hard rule: reputation is earned slowly, one attested task at a time, and can be slashed for fraud, making each fake identity cost more in time and forfeited deposits than it can ever earn.
